posts.headline: Tech-Led Rally Reverses Monday's Losses as AI Fears Ease
posts.body: U.S. markets staged a strong turnaround Tuesday with the Dow gaining 400 points (0.9%), S&P 500 up 0.8%, and Nasdaq rising 1.1% after Monday's AI-driven sell-off. The rebound was led by semiconductor and software stocks recovering from last week's pressure, with the S&P Software & Services index advancing 1.3%. Investor sentiment improved despite lingering tariff uncertainty and Jamie Dimon's warnings about pre-crisis conditions, setting up a pivotal Nvidia earnings tomorrow as the ultimate AI trade test.

posts.headline: Asia-Pac Markets Extend US Rally with Broad Gains
posts.body: Asia-Pacific markets followed Wall Street's positive momentum with Nikkei 225 up 0.87% to 57,321, Hang Seng rising 0.45%, and mainland China's CSI 300 gaining 0.6%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 climbed 1.17% to 9,128.3, while South Korea's Kospi added 1.22%. The region's strength reflects improved AI sentiment and easing concerns about technology disruption risks that had plagued markets last week.

posts.headline: Keysight Technologies Soars 20% on Blowout Results
posts.body: Keysight Technologies (KEYS) surged 20% after Q1 earnings of $2.17/share topped $2.00 estimates with revenue of $1.60B vs. $1.54B expected. The electronics test equipment maker benefited from strong 5G and AI infrastructure spending, making it one of today's top S&P 500 performers. The breakout highlights continued momentum in semiconductor-adjacent plays and suggests the AI supply chain remains robust heading into Nvidia's report.

posts.headline: Planet Fitness, Workday, Lucid Disappoint in After-Hours
posts.body: Planet Fitness (PLNT) fell 5% premarket despite beating revenue estimates, as margin pressure concerned investors. Workday (WDAY) dropped nearly 10% after guiding Q1 subscription revenue below consensus at $2.34B. Lucid Group (LCID) slid 4%+ with a wider-than-expected loss of $3.62/share though revenue topped estimates; the EV maker also cut 12% of its U.S. workforce. These results underscore uneven corporate performance ahead of the pivotal NVDA report.

posts.headline: Nvidia Earnings Tomorrow: AI Market's Biggest Test
posts.body: Nvidia (NVDA) reports Q4 fiscal 2026 earnings after market close Wednesday, with Wall Street expecting $1.45 EPS on $65.7B revenue. The chipmaker faces intense scrutiny after nearly 20% decline in 2026, with analysts forecasting 65%+ revenue growth and 71% EPS increase. Results will be the ultimate barometer for AI spending trends and could trigger major market moves; options pricing suggests an 8-10% swing. The stock is up 2.7% YTD while tech peers remain down double-digits.

posts.headline: Trump's State of the Union Reinforces Tariff Agenda
posts.body: President Trump's Tuesday State of the Union doubled down on trade protectionism, declaring 'we're winning so much' while imposing new tariffs. The administration maintains 15% global tariffs and 50% levies on steel/aluminum/copper, with threats of higher rates for 'game-playing' nations. These policies create uncertainty for multinational companies and could impact supply chains, particularly in tech hardware and automotive sectors in coming months.

posts.headline: Home Depot Beats Despite Housing Market Headwinds
posts.body: Home Depot (HD) delivered an unexpected beat with Q4 EPS of $2.72 vs. $2.54 estimates on revenue of $38.2B, sending shares up 4%. The home improvement giant maintained guidance despite higher interest rates and lower housing turnover, highlighting strength in professional contractor business. The performance suggests consumer resilience on home projects even as big-ticket purchases slow, providing a positive signal for retail discretionary heading into Q1.

posts.headline: NVDA, AMD, and Lowe's Headline Wednesday's Catalysts
posts.body: Wednesday's key events: 1) Nvidia (NVDA) Q4 earnings after close - the most important report of the quarter; 2) Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) saw positive technical action today on Meta AI chips deal; 3) Lowe's (LOW) reports Q4 earnings pre-market, with investor focus on comparison to HD's strong performance; 4) Continued Asia market momentum and any post-SOTU policy announcements. Traders should expect elevated volatility around NVDA results with potential 8-10% overnight move priced in.
